```{python}
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import Markdown

ROOT = Path.cwd().parent
JKP = ROOT / "data" / "jkp"

plt.rcParams.update({"figure.figsize": (6.5, 2.8), "axes.grid": True, "grid.color": "0.9",
                     "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False, "lines.linewidth": 1})
BLUE, GRAY, ORANGE, INK = "#0072B2", "#B0B0B0", "#D55E00", "#333333"  # Okabe-Ito + neutrals

meta = pd.read_csv(JKP / "factor_meta.csv").set_index("factor")
red = pd.read_parquet(JKP / "reduced.parquet")
fr = pd.read_parquet(JKP / "factor_returns_daily.parquet")
stats = pd.read_csv(JKP / "factor_stats.csv", index_col=0)
pca_all = pd.read_csv(JKP / "pca_all.csv")
pca20 = pd.read_csv(JKP / "pca_top20.csv")
picked = pd.read_csv(JKP / "picked_factors.csv", index_col=0)
members = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data" / "universe" / "sp500_universe_early_end.csv",
                      parse_dates=["start_date", "end_date"])


def table(df: pd.DataFrame, digits: int = 4) -> Markdown:
    return Markdown(df.round(digits).to_markdown())
```

Data: JKP global factor model (Jensen, Kelly & Pedersen, *Is There a Replication Crisis in Finance?*), US,
2018-05-01 to 2025-12-31.

- `data/jkp/all.parquet` / `reduced.parquet`: WRDS `contrib.global_factor`, one row per stock per month-end,
  filtered to common stock (CRSP share code 10/11/12), main exchange, primary security. `reduced.parquet` keeps the
  id/return columns plus the 20 picked factors, with the CRSP ticker and a point-in-time S&P 500 flag (`in_sp500`).
- `data/jkp/factor_returns_daily.parquet`: daily long-short returns of the 153 factors (public JKP files, USA,
  capped value weight). Each factor is top tercile minus bottom tercile, signed by `direction` so it is oriented the
  way the original paper found profitable.
- A characteristic at month-end `eom` = t is paired with `ret_exc_lead1m`, the excess return in month t+1.

Generated by `Python/market_data/global_factor_{download,returns,reduce,cov_stats}.py`.

## 1. Stock Panel: Integrity and Coverage

```{python}
red["eom"] = pd.to_datetime(red["eom"])
per_month = red.groupby("eom").agg(stocks=("permno", "size"), sp500=("in_sp500", "sum"))
summary = pd.Series({
    "rows": f"{len(red):,}",
    "columns": red.shape[1],
    "month-ends": red["eom"].nunique(),
    "first / last eom": f"{red['eom'].min().date()} / {red['eom'].max().date()}",
    "distinct stocks (id)": f"{red['id'].nunique():,}",
    "stocks per month (min / median / max)": f"{per_month['stocks'].min():,} / {int(per_month['stocks'].median()):,} / {per_month['stocks'].max():,}",
    "duplicate (id, eom)": int(red.duplicated(["id", "eom"]).sum()),
    "rows without permno (Compustat-only)": f"{red['permno'].isna().mean():.1%}",
    "rows with a CRSP ticker": f"{red['ticker'].notna().mean():.1%}",
    "S&P 500 rows per month (median)": int(per_month["sp500"].median()),
    "ret_exc_lead1m missing": f"{red['ret_exc_lead1m'].isna().mean():.1%}",
}, name="value")
table(summary.to_frame())
```

`ret_exc_lead1m` is missing for the last month (its next-month return is not out yet) and for stocks that delist.

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Point-in-time S&P 500 members (from data/universe) vs. members matched to a JKP row, per month-end."
universe = pd.Series({d: ((members["start_date"] <= d) & (members["end_date"].isna() | (members["end_date"] > d))).sum()
                      for d in per_month.index})
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot(universe.index, universe.values, color=GRAY, label="S&P 500 members")
ax.plot(per_month.index, per_month["sp500"], color=BLUE, label="matched in JKP")
ax.set_ylim(0, 550)
ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="lower right")
plt.show()
```

```{python}
last = per_month.index.max()
norm = lambda s: s.astype(str).str.upper().str.replace(r"[.\-/]", "", regex=True)
active = members[(members["start_date"] <= last) & (members["end_date"].isna() | (members["end_date"] > last))]["ticker"]
have = set(norm(red.loc[red["eom"] == last, "ticker"].dropna()))
if "ticker_cls" in red.columns:
    have |= set(norm(red.loc[red["eom"] == last, "ticker_cls"].dropna()))
missing = sorted(set(norm(active)) - have)
Markdown(f"On {last.date()}, {len(missing)} of {len(active)} S&P 500 members have no JKP row: "
         f"{', '.join(missing)}. Most are REITs (CRSP share code 18), which JKP excludes as non-common stock; "
         "the rest fail the main-exchange or common-stock filter. The risk model has no style exposures for them.")
```

## 2. Characteristic Coverage of the 20 Picked Factors

Share of rows with a non-missing value, for all stocks and for S&P 500 members.

```{python}
cov = pd.DataFrame({
    "cluster": meta.loc[picked.index, "cluster"],
    "all stocks": red[picked.index].notna().mean(),
    "S&P 500": red.loc[red["in_sp500"], picked.index].notna().mean(),
})
table(cov.sort_values("S&P 500"), 3)
```

## 3. Factor Returns

```{python}
summary = pd.Series({
    "trading days": len(fr),
    "first / last day": f"{fr.index.min().date()} / {fr.index.max().date()}",
    "factors": fr.shape[1],
    "missing cells": f"{fr.isna().mean().mean():.2%}",
    "largest absolute daily return": f"{fr.abs().max().max():.2%} ({fr.abs().max().idxmax()})",
    "factors with abs(Newey-West t) > 2": int((stats["t_stat_nw5"].abs() > 2).sum()),
}, name="value")
table(summary.to_frame())
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Cumulative return of the 20 picked factors (gray) and their equal-weight average (blue)."
cum = (1 + fr[picked.index]).cumprod()
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot(cum.index, cum.values, color=GRAY, linewidth=0.6)
ax.plot(cum.index, (1 + fr[picked.index].mean(axis=1)).cumprod(), color=BLUE, linewidth=1.4)
ax.axhline(1, color=INK, linewidth=0.6)
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Annualized Sharpe ratio of the 153 factors by cluster (dots); picked factors in orange."
order = stats.groupby("cluster")["sharpe_ann"].median().sort_values().index
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.5, 3.6))
for i, c in enumerate(order):
    s = stats[stats["cluster"] == c]
    ax.scatter(s["sharpe_ann"], [i] * len(s), s=12, color=np.where(s["picked"], ORANGE, GRAY), zorder=3)
ax.set_yticks(range(len(order)), order, fontsize=8)
ax.axvline(0, color=INK, linewidth=0.6)
ax.set_xlabel("annualized Sharpe ratio")
plt.show()
```

## 4. Covariance and PCA

```{python}
z = np.load(JKP / "cov_cube.npz")
cube, dates = z["cov"], z["dates"]
idx = np.linspace(0, cube.shape[2] - 1, 40).astype(int)
mineig = pd.Series([np.linalg.eigvalsh(cube[:, :, n].astype(float))[0] for n in idx],
                   index=pd.to_datetime(dates[idx]))
summary = pd.Series({
    "cube shape (K, K, N)": str(cube.shape),
    "method / window": f"{z['method']} / {int(z['window'])} days",
    "first / last date": f"{dates[0]} / {dates[-1]}",
    "symmetric": bool(np.allclose(cube[:, :, -1], cube[:, :, -1].T)),
    "min eigenvalue (over 40 sampled dates)": f"{mineig.min():.2e}",
    "condition number (last date)": f"{np.linalg.cond(cube[:, :, -1].astype(float)):.1e}",
}, name="value")
table(summary.to_frame())
```

Every matrix is positive definite, but the smallest eigenvalues are close to zero: the 153 factors are highly
collinear. Use a shrinkage estimator (`--method lw`) or the 20 picked factors in the optimizer.

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Scree plot of the full-sample daily covariance: % of variance explained per PC (bars) and cumulative (line)."
n = 30
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.bar(pca_all["pc"][:n], pca_all["explained_pct"][:n], color=BLUE)
ax2 = ax.twinx()
ax2.plot(pca_all["pc"][:n], pca_all["cumulative_pct"][:n], color=ORANGE, marker=".")
ax2.set_ylim(0, 100)
ax2.grid(False)
ax.axvline(20.5, color=INK, linestyle="--", linewidth=0.6)
ax.set_xlabel("principal component"); ax.set_ylabel("explained %"); ax2.set_ylabel("cumulative %")
plt.show()
```

```{python}
t = pca20[["pc", "lambda_ann", "explained_pct", "cumulative_pct", "top_loadings"]].copy()
t["top_loadings"] = t["top_loadings"].str.split("; ").str[:2].str.join("; ")
t.columns = ["PC", "lambda (ann.)", "expl. %", "cum. %", "top 2 loadings"]
table(t.set_index("PC"), 3)
```

## 5. The 20 Picked Factors

Picked by pivoted QR on the $\sqrt{\lambda}$-scaled top-20 eigenvectors: the 20 original factors whose returns best
span the top-20 principal components. Listed in pick order; Sharpe, volatility and max drawdown are annualized
daily long-short returns, NW t uses 5 Newey-West lags, beta is on the JKP US market factor.

```{python}
r2 = pca20["cumulative_pct"].iloc[-1]
Markdown(f"The top 20 PCs explain {r2:.1f}% of total factor variance. Cluster labels come from JKP's "
         "return-based clustering, so some (e.g. `seas_1_1an` in Profit Growth) differ from the factor name.")
```

```{python}
t = picked.sort_values("rank")[["description"]].join(
    stats[["sharpe_ann", "t_stat_nw5", "vol_ann", "max_drawdown", "beta_mkt"]])
t["description"] = t["description"].str.slice(0, 32)
t.columns = ["description", "Sharpe", "NW t", "vol", "max DD", "beta"]
table(t, 2)
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Correlation of the 20 picked factors' daily returns."
#| fig-height: 5.2
c = fr[picked.index].corr()
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.5, 5.2))
im = ax.imshow(c, cmap="RdBu_r", vmin=-1, vmax=1)
ax.set_xticks(range(len(c)), c.columns, rotation=90, fontsize=7)
```
